items.title: Coordinate maps and permutations are measurable on finite products
items.statement: For measurable coordinate maps into a finite product, the tuple map is measurable; every coordinate permutation of a finite product of one measurable space is measurable.

references.title: John K. Hunter, Measure Theory, §§3.1 and 5.1

items.title: Regular conditional kernels push forward under measurable random maps
items.statement: A regular conditional distribution remains a regular conditional distribution after a jointly measurable map that may depend on the conditioning point; adjoining an independent random element appends its law by product measure.

references.title: John K. Hunter, Measure Theory, §§3.1, 5.1, 5.4–5.5

items.title: Exchangeable random elements
items.statement: A finite tuple of random elements in one measurable space is exchangeable when its joint law is invariant under every coordinate permutation.

references.title: Glenn Shafer and Vladimir Vovk, A Tutorial on Conformal Prediction, JMLR 9 (2008), §3.1
Ryan Tibshirani, Conformal Prediction, Advanced Topics in Statistical Learning, Spring 2024, §1

items.title: Conformal scores and rank p-values
items.statement: Defines measurable split score rules, permutation-equivariant full score assignments, the nonrandomized upper-rank p-value, and the optional tie-randomized p-value using an independent shared uniform variable.

references.title: Jing Lei, Max G'Sell, Alessandro Rinaldo, Ryan J. Tibshirani, and Larry Wasserman, Distribution-Free Predictive Inference for Regression, JASA 113(523) (2018), §§2.1–2.2 and Appendix A.1
Glenn Shafer and Vladimir Vovk, A Tutorial on Conformal Prediction, JMLR 9 (2008), §§3.1, 4.1–4.2
Ryan Tibshirani, Conformal Prediction, Advanced Topics in Statistical Learning, Spring 2024, §§1–3

items.title: Finite order statistics and rank maps are measurable
items.statement: For a finite real score vector, each order statistic, upper-rank p-value, and independent-uniform randomized rank is a Borel-measurable function of its inputs.

references.title: John K. Hunter, Measure Theory, §§3.1 and 5.1

items.title: Permutation-equivariant scores preserve exchangeability
items.statement: A measurable permutation-equivariant score assignment sends an exchangeable data vector to an exchangeable score vector.

references.title: Jing Lei et al., Distribution-Free Predictive Inference for Regression, JASA 113(523) (2018), §2.1 and Remark 2.4
Ryan Tibshirani, Conformal Prediction, Advanced Topics in Statistical Learning, Spring 2024, §3

items.title: Split conformal prediction set
items.statement: For m calibration examples and 0<alpha<1, use k=ceil((m+1)(1-alpha)), the kth calibration score when k<=m and +infinity otherwise, then return candidates with score at most that threshold; an optional exact randomized version uses the shared-U rank p-value.

references.title: Jing Lei et al., Distribution-Free Predictive Inference for Regression, JASA 113(523) (2018), §2.2 and Appendix A.1
Ryan Tibshirani, Conformal Prediction, Advanced Topics in Statistical Learning, Spring 2024, §2

items.title: Full conformal prediction set
items.statement: For each candidate, compute the permutation-equivariant augmented score vector and include the candidate when its nonrandomized upper-rank p-value exceeds alpha, or use the shared-U randomized rank version.

references.title: Jing Lei et al., Distribution-Free Predictive Inference for Regression, JASA 113(523) (2018), §2.1 and Appendix A.1
Glenn Shafer and Vladimir Vovk, A Tutorial on Conformal Prediction, JMLR 9 (2008), §§4.1–4.2
Ryan Tibshirani, Conformal Prediction, Advanced Topics in Statistical Learning, Spring 2024, §3

items.title: Conformal rank superuniformity under exchangeability
items.statement: For an exchangeable real score vector of length n, the nonrandomized upper-rank p-value is superuniform; the specified tie-randomized rank is Uniform(0,1) when its uniform variable is independent.

references.title: Jing Lei et al., Distribution-Free Predictive Inference for Regression, JASA 113(523) (2018), §2.1 and Appendix A.1
Glenn Shafer and Vladimir Vovk, A Tutorial on Conformal Prediction, JMLR 9 (2008), §§3.1, 4.1–4.2
Ryan Tibshirani, Conformal Prediction, Advanced Topics in Statistical Learning, Spring 2024, §§1–2

items.title: Split conformal marginal coverage
items.statement: If the training-fitted score rule is measurable and the calibration and test examples are conditionally exchangeable given the training sigma-field, the split quantile set has conditional and hence marginal coverage at least 1-alpha; the shared-U rank version has conditional and marginal coverage exactly 1-alpha.

references.title: Jing Lei et al., Distribution-Free Predictive Inference for Regression, JASA 113(523) (2018), Theorem 2.2 and Appendix A.1
Ryan Tibshirani, Conformal Prediction, Advanced Topics in Statistical Learning, Spring 2024, §2

items.title: Full conformal marginal coverage
items.statement: For exchangeable examples and a measurable permutation-equivariant score assignment, full conformal has marginal coverage at least 1-alpha; independent shared-U randomized ties give exact marginal coverage 1-alpha.

references.title: Jing Lei et al., Distribution-Free Predictive Inference for Regression, JASA 113(523) (2018), Theorem 2.1, Remark 2.4, and Appendix A.1
Glenn Shafer and Vladimir Vovk, A Tutorial on Conformal Prediction, JMLR 9 (2008), §§4.1–4.2
Ryan Tibshirani, Conformal Prediction, Advanced Topics in Statistical Learning, Spring 2024, §3

title: Conformal Prediction and Exchangeable Ranks — Examples

items.title: Split conformal coverage can be conservative when scores tie
items.statement: With three identical exchangeable scores, m=2 and alpha=1/2, the nonrandomized split quantile set covers with probability 1, while the specified independent-uniform rank randomization covers with probability 1/2.

items.title: Full conformal ranks a candidate in an augmented sample
items.statement: For a uniformly random ordering of the fixed distinct score multiset {1,2,3}, an equivariant identity-score assignment gives the true candidate upper p-value 1, 2/3, or 1/3, each with probability 1/3; at alpha=0.4 the coverage is 2/3.

items.title: Marginal split coverage need not give rare-subgroup coverage
items.statement: A split conformal rule can satisfy its marginal lower bound under exchangeability while its conditional coverage on a rare group is below the nominal level.

items.title: Exchangeability failure can destroy split coverage
items.statement: A calibration sample drawn entirely at label 0 and a test label fixed at 1 yield zero coverage for a simple split score set, so the exchangeability hypothesis cannot be dropped.
